facts.raw_span: An 89-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation (not anticoagulated) and hypertension
presented with acute speech disturbance and right-sided weakness
global aphasia, right facial asymmetry, right upper- and lower-limb paresis with decreased tone, and a right Babinski sign
NIH Stroke Scale score was 19
Noncontrast head CT showed early ischemic changes in the left insula and frontal lobe
CT angiography revealed acute occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery at M1/M2 and chronic occlusion of the left internal carotid artery
elevated C-reactive protein (10.74 mg/dL) and procalcitonin (0.11 ng/mL)
cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed mild pleocytosis (10 cells/µL) and elevated protein (55 mg/dL)
severe low-gradient aortic stenosis with preserved ejection fraction
no history of COVID-19
RT-PCR testing for SARS-CoV-2 on admission and hospital day 3 was negative
pulmonary emboli in segmental arteries of the right lower lobe
